americas_summary: The Americas face high exposure through oil/LNG pricing, freight and import delays, critical-mineral availability, and tighter financial conditions. No evidence shows broad Americas fuel rationing, port closure, payment outage, or banking-access restrictions.
confidence_rationale: Fresh, multi-source evidence directly documents maritime disruption, mineral constraints, financial-market stress, and U.S. health activity; several pivotal reports are syndicated tier-C sources and some effects remain prospective. Evidence gate: 15 items, 11 sources, 4 Tier-A sources, 5/5 clusters.
summary: Severe, observed maritime-energy disruption at Hormuz and persistent Red Sea impairment remain the primary civilian-risk drivers, with spillovers to energy prices, freight, trade, and supply chains. U.S.-China critical-mineral constraints add targeted technology and manufacturing exposure; financial conditions remain stressed but without access restrictions.
primary_driver: Near-stalling Hormuz shipping after tanker attacks, compounded by sustained Red Sea shipping disruption.
primary_stabilizers: Oil prices fell Friday as possible U.S.-Iran truce discussions partly offset concerns that Houthi attacks could disrupt Saudi energy supplies.
Washington and Beijing are seeking overall stability despite continuing blacklists and restrictions on high-tech products and critical-mineral trade.
U.S. and Venezuelan officials discussed sovereign-debt restructuring, providing a diplomatic channel that could reduce financial and governance stress if sustained.
Countries completed a WHO simulation of a cross-border poultry food-safety emergency, testing coordination between health authorities and food-safety networks.

signals.title: Hormuz shipping nearly stalls
signals.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz nearly halted after attacks on three UAE-operated tankers, sharply increasing disruption risk for oil and LNG flows.

signals.title: Red Sea threats persist
signals.summary: Saudi Arabia reported thwarting Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh and Yanbu, while monitors said Red Sea shipping remained well below prewar levels.

signals.title: Rare-earth shipments remain constrained
signals.summary: Some Chinese suppliers reportedly declined U.S. rare-earth shipments, while yttrium, indium phosphide, and tungsten remained expensive amid tight supply.

signals.title: Treasury sell-off intensifies
signals.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.12% and the 30-year yield 5.44%, amid a broad government-bond sell-off and concerns over inflation and debt trajectories.

signals.title: Bank-sector pressure remains
signals.summary: U.S. financial stocks fell sharply, with the S&P 500 financial index down 2% and the bank index down 3% on September 22.

signals.title: U.S. measles burden
signals.summary: CDC reported 3,294 confirmed U.S. measles cases by September 10, with 95% outbreak-associated, indicating sustained transmission and ongoing community-health pressure.

signals.title: Kīlauea activity resumes
signals.summary: Kīlauea’s summit eruption produced renewed lava overflows, while USGS maintained WATCH and aviation ORANGE; activity remained confined to Halemaʻumaʻu crater.

preparedness_actions: Complete sensible, previously planned preparedness purchases while normal supply channels are functioning.
Maintain several weeks of food, household consumables, water capacity, and essential medical supplies.
Keep vehicles reasonably fueled and verify generator, battery, solar, or other backup-power capability.
Maintain diversified payment options and a reasonable amount of emergency cash.
Confirm family communications, transportation, and meeting plans.
Avoid panic buying; focus on resilience gaps that would be difficult to correct after disruption begins.

methodology.note: All-hazards early-warning assessment. The score is a preparedness-urgency index, not the probability that a disaster, collapse, or war will occur.
methodology.formula: Preparedness Urgency = 40% Global Threat Pressure + 25% Observed Civilian Disruption + 10% Cross-System Coupling + 10% Momentum/Persistence + 15% Americas Exposure. Global threat, observed impact, and Americas exposure are weighted averages across all 12 domains.
methodology.rate_limits: Absent a verified hard trigger, normal daily movement is limited to ±3 points. A verified but non-severe hard trigger allows up to ±6. A verified national, multinational, or global hard trigger can bypass the rate limit.
methodology.stage_guardrails: HIGH ALERT begins at 80. IMMINENT DISRUPTION requires a score of at least 90, observed disruption of at least 75, and a verified severe hard trigger plus either 48-hour persistence or an active fast-onset trigger. ACTIVE DISRUPTION requires at least 97, observed disruption at least 85, three high-impact domains, and two verified severe triggers.
methodology.civil_unrest: Civil Unrest / Public Order is scored from observable violence, duration, geographic spread, emergency measures, infrastructure damage, and disruption to transport, commerce, public safety, or essential services. Peaceful protest and political ideology do not raise the score by themselves.
methodology.confidence: Evidence confidence is capped mechanically by source quality, recency, independence, cluster coverage, and actual web-search completion. It does not increase preparedness urgency.
methodology.pipeline: GPT-5.6 Luna collects current evidence in paced, low-context, one-search cluster requests to stay below TPM limits. GPT-5.6 Terra evaluates only validated evidence with no web access. JavaScript validates hard triggers and calculates the final score mechanically.
